We REALLY need Microsoft to lose this case. Before you jump down my throat, hear me out:

If Microsoft loses, then the US can get records from a US headquartered business with a warrant (due process of law). This does not fundamentally alter our common sense understanding of legal search and seizure. The physical location of data on the cloud is irrelevant, the important thing is who the data belongs to, much like a search of your physical mail.

Then consider the precedent if Microsoft wins. Data itself would be considered to have nationality apart from that data's owner. This means there would be a very easy legal argument justifying the blanket seizure of all data as it crosses out of and into the US. After all, while it is outside the US, it isn't subject to US law, and thus isn't protected by the 4th amendment (no due process of law). Sound familiar?

So which would you rather have: the government being able to get access to your data with a warrant (like they can with everything else you own)? Or would you prefer they be able to take advantage of the global nature of the cloud to have legitimate legal standing for stealing all your data?

With those choices, I will hope that Microsoft loses this one.
